newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross says relief actions approved by Taleban.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross says relief actions approved by Taleban.

text.p: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said on Friday the Taleban forces in control of the Afghan capital Kabul had agreed it could continue humanitarian relief operations.

Senior ICRC official Jean-Pierre Monod told reporters a Taleban military commander had given the go-ahead -- including approval for a 35-truck relief convoy -- during a meeting earlier in the day with an ICRC representative in the city.
"We have to continue our work to help victims of the conflict," Monod told a news conference.

"We have been helping around a quarter of a million people in Kabul, about 25 per cent of the city's population. And with the winter coming nothing indicates that this number will diminish -- on the contrary, we might be facing an even worse emergency."
Monod, in overall charge of ICRC operations in Asia, said a convoy bringing 300 tonnes of food was due to leave Peshawar in Pakistan on Sunday for the Afghan capital.

The Swiss-run ICRC, which has 15 expatriate staff in Kabul including several women, had been assured it could continue working in city hospitals and had enough medical supplies already in stock there to meet all current needs.

Monod indicated there was no early sign that the Taleban, who have declared they would enforce a strict Islamic system severely restricting the activities of women and girls outside the home, would put limits on its female expatriate staff.

He told the news conference that in the southern city of Kandahar, controlled by the movement for the past year, Taleban officials had allowed a foreign ICRC woman surgeon to treat men as well as women.

"We have a team of 17 people, eight of whom are ladies, and they are working normally and are accepted," he said. "It is a matter of explaining to the Taleban why there is no option...It is a matter of being pragmatic and making sure that the job is being done, and is well done," he declared.
But Afghan women nurses employed by the ICRC had been restricted there to working in female wards.

Monod told the news conference a "major disaster" had been avoided in Kabul by the decision of the administration of President Burhanuddin Rabbani to pull its forces out and not fight the Taleban on the streets of the already-devastated city.
And he said the ICRC hoped for humanitarian reasons that the ousted government would not try to retake it by force.
"I hope that they will have the wisdom to find another way to interact with the Taleban than to provoke new battles for Kabul which would mean attacking the city again from the outside," he declared.
